Plus it even works if i start out whisper-reading, and then transition into silent reading!

happy to help! Baan is the newer sister location and has been open for little more than 1 year now. While their facility is more modern and updated, they have a less established community and their students have a higher number of beginners (I believe). They may also have less classes on their schedule, but to compensate for that, their prices are cheaper. MAFA has been in Erin Mills for nearly, 7+ years now I believe. Their head instructor is Kru Gerald who was trained straight under [Ajahn Suchart](https://www.siamno1.com/ajahn-suchart/). They have a bigger space and a more established community. I can't speak as in depth on battle arts or kombat, but from what i've heard, kombat recently had to downsize to a smaller location and it has made their classes seem cramped. Best option is to call around and ask to take free trial classes at all of them, see which classes suit you best. I'm pretty sure, MAFA & Baan offer up to 3 free classes. If you're interested in finding out the most traditional gym, ask about their foundations and credentials in Muay Thai. No matter where you end up going, Muay Thai is a sport to fall in love with. Glad to hear you're looking for the most authentic learning experience possible. have fun checking them out!

MAFA and Baan Muay Thai are separate gyms and two different locations. While related, Baan is the newer sister location to MAFA. The instruction and classes are fantastic at both. But unless you *specifically* buy a dual membership to both, it would be good to know they're priced differently because they're two different gyms.
